name: Dakhla Lagoon
hero_subtitle: A 40 km turquoise lagoon between Sahara dunes and the Atlantic — the geographic and sporting heart of Dakhla.

overview.title: The lagoon that defines Dakhla
overview.p1: Dakhla’s lagoon stretches for roughly forty kilometres along a sand peninsula. Sheltered from open-ocean swell, its shallow turquoise water stays remarkably flat — the reason the world comes here to kitesurf and wingfoil.
overview.p2: Even without a board, the lagoon is the main stage: boat trips, oyster farms, flamingos in season, and light that shifts from silver to deep blue across the day.
overview.p3: Most camps and schools sit on the lagoon shore. Town is a short drive; the White Dune and Dragon Island are classic lagoon outings.

tips.title: Practical Tips for Visiting Dakhla Lagoon

1.title: Getting Around
1.desc: Taxis or rental cars are needed to reach the various lagoon camps and spots down the peninsula from Dakhla town.

2.title: Sun & Wind Protection
2.desc: The combination of desert sun and steady coastal wind means high SPF sunscreen, sunglasses, and a windbreaker are essential.

3.title: Tides & Nature
3.desc: Be mindful of changing tides when walking on the flats, and respect local wildlife areas and protected bird habitats.

q1.question: Is Dakhla Lagoon free to visit?
q1.answer: Yes, accessing the shores of the lagoon is completely free. Costs apply only if you rent water sports equipment, book boat excursions, or dine at the oyster farms and camps.

q2.question: What is the best time to visit the lagoon?
q2.answer: Early morning offers the calmest glass-like water and stunning sunrise colors, while late afternoon provides magical golden light reflecting across the tidal flats.

q3.question: Can I see wildlife at Dakhla Lagoon?
q3.answer: Yes! The lagoon is a protected Ramsar site and a crucial stop for migratory birds, including large flocks of flamingos, herons, and waders.

q4.question: What are the local culinary specialties here?
q4.answer: Dakhla is famous for its fresh local oysters farmed directly in the clean waters of the lagoon, as well as fresh Atlantic fish and traditional Saharan mint tea.

q5.question: How far is the lagoon from Dakhla town?
q5.answer: The main kite camps and central areas of the lagoon are located along the peninsula, roughly a 20 to 30-minute drive from downtown Dakhla.
